findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Observed there was not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) when the inspector arrived. The employee working stated they had taken the test but they could not provide any proof to the inspector. During the inspection a CFPM arrived at the facility. Ensure that a CFPM is present during all hours of operation by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed an employee wash hands and turn off the faucet with their bare hands. The employee was educated on the proper hand washing procedure when the action was observed. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed a cutting board and pizza peel stored behind the faucet of the triple sink. Storing utensils in this position presents the risk of contamination from water splashes, food residue, or other types of debris. The PIC removed the utensils from this position during the inspection. Ensure that food contact surfaces are always clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following are not clean to sight and touch:

(1) The dusty hood system. 

(2) The food debris in the prep cooler bottom. 

(3) The dirty tray to the right of the oven  - COS; the PIC replaced the tray during the inspection. 

Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that employees do not have food handler certificates. All food handles who do not have CFPM certificates must obtain training in basic food handling principles. Ensure that all required employees obtain food handler certificates by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed an employee fail to use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The inspector educated the employee when the action was observed. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet after hand washing to avoid re-contaminating clean hands. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed the staff working did not have food handler training completed. All food handlers, other than those with Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) certificates, must obtain training in basic food handling principles. Ensure that all food handlers obtain the training by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed base coving in the back warewashing area which has peeled off the wall. There is some water damage to the wall in that corner and cracked tiles. All surfaces subject to water/food penetration must be SMOOTH, NON-ABSORBENT AND EASILY CLEANABLE. Ensure that thes surfaces are repaired/replaced by the next routine inspection. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that a pizza peel was stored underneath the rack on the front counter against the east wall. The rack and peel were removed, cleaned and sanitized and replaced. Corrected on site. Ensure that in-use utensils are stored in clean, dry, sanitized locations. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Two mops were observed sitting on the floor and in the bottom of a mop bucket. Only the mop stored in the bottom of the mop bucket was wet. No water was present in the mop bucket. Mops must be stored inverted or in the top portion of a mop bucket to facilitate air drying and prevent contamination/pest harborage conditions. The mops were hung correctly during the inspection. Corrected on site. Ensure that mops are stored properly in the future. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: Observed the hand sink near the 3 part sink to have various items inside it. Ensure the hand sink is used for hand washing only. The items were removed during the inspection.
(B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.
